items.title: MECH-428/INV-086 waypoint_field_consumer_reach H2 (representation axis): does the SD-WAYPOINT-FIELD signal survive REE's observation-to-z_world compression?
items.note: H2 (representation axis) of the GOV-FANOUT-1 two-leg waypoint_field_consumer_reach portfolio pre-registered by the confirmed failure_autopsy_V3-EXQ-1004_2026-09-05 (section 7a; registry qid waypoint_field_consumer_reach, hid H-wpfield-zworld-interface). H1 (drive axis, objective/exploration) is the sibling leg, queued separately -- one experiment per session. QUESTION: does the SD-WAYPOINT-FIELD directional signal, shown decodable and behaviourally sufficient for a supervised reader over the RAW observation by V3-EXQ-1004 (0.575 -> 0.841 BC-imitation accuracy), survive REE's OWN observation-to-z_world compression, or is it lost before it reaches E1/E2/E3? DECLARED NULL: the z_world accuracy lift (ON-OFF) is indistinguishable from zero while the raw-observation lift is large -- locates the loss at the encoder. DESIGN: 2 arms (field_off/field_on) x 5 seeds. Per cell: SD-070 P0a generic encoder warmup (run_zworld_p0, unrelated to waypoints) on a dedicated env -> freeze the whole latent stack -> random-policy rollout on a second dedicated env, collecting (z_world, raw narrow radius-2-waypoint-channel-plus-field slice, oracle 5-way direction label) per step -> fit fresh single-layer linear probes (cross-entropy, EPISODE-level 80/20 split) predicting the label from each feature. LOAD-BEARING C1: on >=3/5 seeds, z_world lift is within +/-0.05 (one-sided-safe null band) -> PASS = H2 supported (lost at encoder); a positive lift beyond the band -> FAIL 'survives'; a negative lift beyond the band -> FAIL 'anomalous_negative_lift' (flagged, not read as either survives or lost); no seed-count majority in any direction -> FAIL 'inconsistent_across_seeds'. READINESS (not claim evidence, self-routes substrate_not_ready_requeue below floor): R1 raw-observation lift (same statistic C1 reads, on the SAME narrow 1004-style slice, NOT the full world_state -- a pilot check found the full vector collapses the lift to ~0.06-0.09 via resource/hazard proximity fields the manipulation never touches) clears 0.15 on >=3/5 seeds; R2 world encoder actually moved during warmup (all 10 cells); R3 a z_world grid-quadrant auxiliary probe (agent position, structurally present regardless of the field) clears 0.55 on >=6/10 cells -- confirms the SAME fitting procedure can extract a KNOWN signal from z_world's own scale/distribution, so a small waypoint-direction lift means the field specifically was not decodable, not that the pipeline extracts nothing at all. CLAIMS: INV-086/MECH-428 evidence_direction_per_claim = non_contributory UNCONDITIONALLY (read-across only per the confirmed 1004 autopsy's instruction for this fan-out -- no REE agent doing subgoal-mode navigation, no z_goal, no feedback-channel ablation, no forced-seed control; neither claim's own hypothesis is exercised regardless of the z_world verdict). GOV-REUSE-1 (2.4): reanalysis_query.py --readout waypoint_zworld_decodability checked against v3_exq_1004 (substrate_hash 9a9fbe795140370f) and v3_exq_884_mech428 (0091fba4d567a1ae) -- 0/2 carry it -> not recoverable, run. Re-derive brake (2.5b): INV-086 = 0 hits, MECH-428 = 1 hit (failure_autopsy_V3-EXQ-884_2026-08-03) -- below threshold 2, does not fire. Substrate gate (2.5c): waypoint-proximity-field-observable RELEASED by the confirmed 1004 autopsy's user gate 2026-09-05 (status implemented_validated, severity corrupting->degrading; confirmed live in substrate_queue.json before queuing) -- this run's own H1/H2 fan-out is exactly what the release un-gated. Checked every OTHER open substrate_queue entry for overlap with this driver's exercised code (ree_core/agent.py, causal_grid_world.py, utils/config.py, latent/stack.py, latent/zworld_p0.py): three OPEN `corrupting` entries share a file this driver imports (contextmemory-write-path-addressing-degeneracy, sd_blocked_agency_mismatch_floor_calibration, sd105_frozen_shared_entropy_floor_multiplier) but each one's specific defective code path is gated behind a config flag that defaults OFF and is never set by this driver (sd016_writepath_mode='off' so ContextMemory.write() is never called -- agent.py:5386-5397 confirmed by source read; use_blocked_agency=False; use_selection_entropy_floor=False) -- verified inert, not exercised, so the corrupting stop-gate does not apply. Two OPEN `degrading` entries (SD-018, SD-106) concern OPTIONAL amend legs of the exact zworld_p0.py recipe this driver uses (resource_field_weight, preservation_weight) -- both default 0.0/OFF and never enabled here (this driver passes no config= override to run_zworld_p0, so it gets the legacy/default recipe only). Two further OPEN `degrading` entries name causal_grid_world.py (mech357-freeze-incompatible- pressure-mechanism, SD-MECH303-THRESHOLD-SOURCING) for hazard-pursuit-onboarding / contextual-safety-harm-threshold mechanisms this driver's DV does not depend on (noted for the record only). dv-dynamic-range-precondition-class (degrading) is the p0_readiness_gate/dv_headroom_check framework itself, status implemented_pending_ validation -- this driver's own readiness gates rely on infrastructure not yet independently validated; noted, not a reason to withhold. STEP 4.5 RED-TEAM (fable-5.1, cross-model, one pass): CONTESTED, 6 findings, ALL verified against source and fixed (full dispositions in the module docstring): F1 an under-fit/scale-starved z_world probe could satisfy the null by construction -> added R3 quadrant auxiliary positive control. F2 (the significant one) OFF/ON built INDEPENDENTLY-SIZED (250/275-dim) agents from different RNG draws -- an unpaired contrast between two random networks, not a content-only ON/OFF comparison -> _FieldMaskedEnv now always builds the WIDE env and zero-masks world_state's trailing 25 dims under OFF (1004's own F7 zero-pad convention, extended from the raw-slice probe to the agent's actual z_world input); both arms now byte-identical at init for a seed. F3 abs(lift)<=ceiling folded a strongly NEGATIVE lift into the same 'survives' label as a genuine positive lift, the opposite claim -> three-way outcome split (survives / anomalous_negative / inconsistent). F4 z_world is a 0.9-EMA over within-episode state (stack.py:1584) so a step-level random train/test split leaked temporally-adjacent same-episode samples across the split, inflating apparent decodability -> episode-level 80/20 split. F5(a) verified by source read: agent.sense() feeds world_obs_encoder(world_state) (agent.py:4802, a separate NEVER-trained random Linear+ReLU) into split_encoder.world_encoder, but P0a (zworld_p0.py::_z_world_path) trains split_encoder.world_encoder directly on RAW world_state -- a genuine train/eval mismatch, but a PRE-EXISTING corpus-wide SD-070 characteristic shared by every driver using run_zworld_p0+agent.sense() and out of this session's scope to fix (a shared, already-validated recipe 5 sibling drivers depend on) -> recorded a second non-load-bearing diagnostic probe (zworld_direct_probe, split_encoder.world_encoder(raw) directly) so a later reader can attribute a null to either stage. F5(b) 'encoder moved' is a weak positive since field values are bounded away from zero in-bounds, so Adam almost certainly perturbs those columns regardless of whether the objective preserves their content -> recorded column-wise weight-delta split at the field-dims boundary as a diagnostic. F6 (minor) MIN_TEST_SAMPLES now enforced; probe Linear init seeded independently of ambient global RNG; probe env uses a distinct seed offset from the warmup env (two envs built from the identical seed reproduce the identical episode-layout sequence). No second red-team pass per the one-pass rule -- all six were CONTESTED with concrete confirmers, none BLOCKING. Smoke: dry-run PASS end-to-end (validate_experiments.py --strict: 0 warnings except the advisory, non-blocking anchor-reachability lint -- left unexempted per that tool's own guidance since EXEMPT requires the predicate to BE the degeneracy definition, not the case for a first-of-lineage count/fraction statistic; reachability instead demonstrated empirically via a below-budget 2-seed pilot on the POST-fix design, raw lift 0.42/0.15 vs z_world lift 0.057/0.023 -- not evidence, a below-budget reachability check only). Timed one full-budget cell at ~68s; 10 cells -> ~11-12 min, estimated_minutes set with headroom.
